records.title: x402 reference client signs any server-declared 402 amount (overcharge vector)
records.summary: The reference x402 client signs and submits payment for ANY amount the server declares in 402 payment requirements, with no verification against the resource's canonical price. A server that inflated the requirement 10x was paid the inflated amount in 3/3 reproduced sessions on Base Sepolia (client authorized 100,000 units = 0.1 USDC for a resource priced at 10,000 units = 0.01 USDC). The only protection is the caller-configured spend limit (maxAmountPerPayment), which a modest overcharge passes easily.

records.notes: Closes the #3866 reviewer round-2 asks (NSPG13 2026-10-22; TKCollective 2026-10-24): (1) unchanged-quote positive case WITH control mode enabled — signs x2, zero rejections, gate does not break the honest case; (2) per-field change battery — payTo rejected by control before signer, asset/network rejected by the client's own spendControls (observe-mode mirrors prove the built-in guard), resource/method change = new binding with caller-expectation coverage; (3) mid-session price DROP (bait-down) rejected before signer; (4) anchor integrity — a rejected quote never becomes the accepted anchor (signer x0, rejected x2); (5) case semantics renamed: quote-change sessions are two completed mocked cycles, not a lost-response retry. records.title: S-BS-14/15 wave 2.5 — binding-race & non-atomic-amount first run (lab probes A10a/A10b/A11, x402 PR #3920 @ 2b4cc47)

subject.sut_note: PR #3920 @ 2b4cc47 (client-side spend-controls candidate fix): @x402/fetch + @x402/core + @x402/evm 2.28.0 pinned, spendControls enabled (default maxAmountPerPayment $1); instrumented at the signer boundary (signer-call counter + resolved-payload.amount inspection, no catch-pattern); adversarial resource server is Argus-owned (fault-injection stand, settlement mocked, unfunded one-shot wallet)

scenarios.name: BindingRace
scenarios.checks: race A10a (explicit expectation) + A10b (first-accepted): BOTH EIP-3009 payloads signed at divergent payTo before any binding was recorded (signer x2) — candidate-fix boundary; control-1 sequential pair, fresh client: exactly 1 signer call, attempt 2 rejected pre-signer (QuoteMismatchError) — green; control-2 parallel identical pair: 2 signed payloads, no false positive — green; fixed-client positive control (binding before attempt 2) → PASS with controls green

scenarios.name: NonAtomicAmount
scenarios.checks: decimal "0.5" signed at enabled pin $0.01 (×50, under the default $1 cap; resolved payload.amount = 500000) — candidate-fix boundary; control-1 cap shield "2" ($2, over cap): rejected pre-signer, 0 calls — green; control-2 atomic duplicate "500000": QuoteMismatchError pre-signer, 0 calls — green; cap=false opt-in variant "100000.5" signed (exploit window is UNDER the cap)

findings_summary.title: State-init TOCTOU (binding race): two concurrent requirement sets on one quota key — client signs BOTH payloads at divergent payTo before the binding is recorded (candidate-fix boundary of PR #3920 @ 2b4cc47; parent axis x402#3866, registry finding #0000)
Non-atomic decimal amount "0.5" bypasses the ENABLED pin check: payload signed at ×50 the pin, under the default cap (same class unprobed: S-BS-15b/c exponential/hex/v1 maxAmountRequired)

records.title: Inngest idempotency conformance battery — 13 probes, 0 FAIL (2 DX findings filed inngest/inngest#5091)

subject.sut_note: SUT = unmodified npm dist packages; runtime-side verification via inngest-cli@1.49.0 dev server, local only (Gate D: CLI is SSPL 1.0 + Apache 2.0 Future License, sha256 300ec5a8..., verified pre-run; no vendor-operated service touched). Probe rules pre-registered in harness app.mjs header before the run. Run #2 (2026-10-26T20:24:53Z) is canonical: run #1 (2026-10-26T19:33Z) produced identical verdicts; run #1 raw evidence lost to a lab environment reset

scenarios.name: InngestH1Static
scenarios.checks: 5 probes, in-process via the vendor's own @inngest/test harness. I1 PASS: replay of a completed step returns the memoized result, body not re-run. I2/I4 OBSERVED: commit-then-throw and lost-memo crash model re-execute the step body — matches the vendor's blog FAQ and docs idempotency page nearly verbatim. I3/I3b OBSERVED: memo keyed by userland step ID without payload binding; parallel branches reusing one step ID execute independently — ID model documented under 'Keep step IDs stable'

scenarios.name: InngestI5Dynamic
scenarios.checks: 8 probes against the local dev server with a crash-safe external effect ledger. p0 PASS: baseline memo integrity, 1 charge. p4b/p4c/p4d PASS: documented event-ID dedup holds under a 12-way concurrent race (1 run / 1 charge), under sequential reuse (0 runs), fresh-ID control fires exactly once. p1/p2 OBSERVED: true A3 window reproduced live — provider commits, then step body throws (retry, ~24.5s backoff) or process.exit(1) (supervisor restart) — 2 charges, exactly as the vendor discloses. p3 OBSERVED (refined): duplicate step ID across parallel chains is warned (AUTOMATIC_PARALLEL_INDEXING) and auto-indexed into a separate memo slot, both handlers execute. p4a OBSERVED: 12 concurrent sends without a shared event ID produce 12 independent runs, the documented per-event model

findings_summary.title: @inngest/test does not surface AUTOMATIC_PARALLEL_INDEXING or any execution warnings: tests pass silently on code the runtime explicitly flags as a footgun
@inngest/test MockedStep memo injection is keyed by userland step ID and bypasses runtime collision indexing (auto-indexed keys unreachable from the test engine), with no divergence flag

Commit-then-crash window (external effect lands before memo write; retry re-runs the body) is documented by the vendor (docs idempotency page 'Verify the behavior', blog FAQ) and confirmed to behave exactly as documented; the vendor's prescribed mitigations (event-ID dedup; idempotency key at the external call) verified effective under a 12-way concurrent race

records.notes: Scope: single-node dev server; idempotency claim surface per vendor docs, methodology anchored to the vendor's own 'Verify the behavior' checklist. Multi-node/cloud dedup semantics, flow control, timers/cron, retry-exhaustion terminal states, and payment-rail scenarios are out of scope for this cycle (no vendor cloud engagement). Verdict taxonomy: PASS = platform held beyond the documented scenarios; OBSERVED = observed behavior matches the vendor's published disclosure. Neither attests bug-freeness.
